content.text:
I opened PR #56 (https://github.com/cv/pi-action/pull/56) with four commits. It covers prompt templates, the two new tool inputs, and override logging. `npm run check` passes, and every commit passes commitlint.

1. **`feat: log when an extension replaces a tool, and test overrides`**
   - Extensions could already replace and wrap tools; this documents and tests it.
   - If an extension has a tool with the same name as an earlier one, the later tool replaces it. The log now says `pi-durable extension X replaces tool bash from coding-tools`.
   - There was no `src/thread.test.ts`, so I added one. It checks the default tool list, that wraps of `bash` and of a pit-style section apply in input order (the last wrap wins), that a wrap with `callers: ["tools"]` hides a tool from the model, and that a later tool replaces one with the same name.

2. **`feat: add exclude_tools and model_tools_hidden inputs`**
   - `exclude_tools` turns a tool off completely: neither the model nor other tools can call it.
   - `model_tools_hidden` keeps a tool away from the model, but other tools (such as pit's `tools.*`) can still call it.
   - Both accept `*` globs and are checked against the tools that exist after the extensions and their wraps are installed.
   - A name that matches no tool gives a warning. If no tools are left for the model, the run fails.
   - The inputs are applied on every run, so an empty input clears what an earlier run set.
   - The `🤖` log line now lists the tools the model gets.

3. **`feat: expand prompt templates from extensions, the project, and agent_dir`**
   - When the text after `@pi` starts with `/<name>` and a template has that name, it is replaced by the template body with the arguments filled in (`$1`…, `$ARGUMENTS`/`$@`, `${@:N[:L]}`, `${ARGUMENTS:-default}`).
   - Templates come from each package's `pi.prompts` (including pi-durable packages), then `.pi/prompts` only with `trust_project`, then `<agent_dir>/prompts`. If two have the same name, the first wins and the others get a warning.
